content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato tots are small, deep‑fried or baked balls made from grated sweet potato, often seasoned and coated with breadcrumbs. They have a crispy exterior and a soft, slightly sweet interior characteristic of sweet potatoes. Tots are popular as a snack or side in fast‑food restaurants, quick‑serve eateries, and street‑food stalls.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes are richer in beta‑carotene than regular potatoes, giving the tots a bright orange hue.
Sweet potato tots gained popularity in the United States in the early 2000s as a healthier alternative to traditional potato croquettes.
Some recipes add corn starch to the mixture to create an extra‑crunchy crust.
Tots are often served with yogurt‑based dips, salsa, or honey‑mustard sauces.
Sweet potatoes are grown in tropical and subtropical regions, but are available year‑round in many countries.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Lower glycemic index than regular potatoes
items.content: Sweet potato tots cause a slower rise in blood sugar compared with regular potato fries.

items.title: Source of potassium and vitamin C
items.content: These nutrients help maintain heart health and antioxidant defenses.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Antioxidants help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sweet potato allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to sweet potatoes.

items.title: High calorie content when fried
items.content: Because tots are often deep‑fried, they can be calorie‑dense; moderation is advised.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Added salt or sauces can increase sodium intake, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve sweet potato tots hot as a snack, side dish for burgers, or in a lunch box. Dip them in yogurt, garlic aioli, honey‑mustard, or spicy chili sauce. For a lighter option, bake them in the oven instead of frying.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked tots in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Uncooked, frozen tots keep for up to 2 months; thaw and fry or bake before serving.
